title: Daisugi, the Japanese technique of growing trees out of other trees (2020)
summary: Daisugi is an ancient Japanese forestry technique dating back to the 15th century, where cedar trees are cultivated by cutting a mature tree and allowing new shoots to grow from the stump, creating a 'tree growing from a tree'. This sustainable method from Kyoto produces straight, knot-free timber ideal for construction without requiring full tree removal or replanting.
problem_solved: Provides sustainable timber production that maintains forest ecosystems while producing high-quality straight-grain wood for traditional Japanese architecture.
why_valuable: Demonstrates how ancient agricultural wisdom offers modern lessons in sustainable resource management and living systems design.
